findings.summary: Historical-result carry-forward rejects legitimate active traceability additions after the checkpoint.
findings.evidence: _traceability_matches_checkpoint requires every live file under work/<work-id>/traceability to equal the checkpoint snapshot exactly. Normal traceability runs append results and execution rows without publishing a new inner-loop checkpoint (see .agents/ask/verification/traceability/adapters.py:74-80). When a prior integrated TaskResult has an older contract_sha, inspect invokes this comparison during its scope-compatible carry-forward path; any valid later task run makes it return false, causing TaskResult contract identity mismatch and blocking state transactions/integration. This contradicts the requested behavior that traceability divergence prevent carry-forward only for untrusted edits without blocking normal active traceability updates.
findings.requested_change: Preserve exact checkpointed historical rows and reports, but allow validated append-only run artifacts for the active accepted task/contract; alternatively provide a coordinator-owned checkpoint publication path for those normal updates that does not depend on the stale-result check it is trying to resolve. Add a regression test that appends a valid active-plan run after checkpoint publication and confirms the old result remains carry-forward eligible, while edits to retained historical artifacts still require recovery.

summary: T56 now validates a digest-bound retained final-Green report for every old scoped test ID, rejects changed accepted specs, and rejects post-checkpoint traceability tampering. However, its whole-directory equality check also rejects normal later traceability appends, blocking the active CR-2 path while the earlier integrated CR-1 result has an older contract identity.
